gen-dafont-galaxy-noto-serif: Galaxy draws every letter with one uninterrupted line width, tall and dense in the lowercase and loosely fitted, like a cosmic signboard. Noto Serif follows with a gentle thick-thin rhythm that carries long paragraphs smoothly.
gen-dafont-good-times-lora: Commanding and geometric, Good Times stacks its small letters tall and heavy, with an e that keeps a clear gap. Lora brings the bookish warmth, its hairline curves and welcoming c giving the pair its strongest quality.
gen-dafont-good-times-noto-serif: Tall, cable-thick small letters and a gapped e give Good Times a look nobody could mistake for anything else. Noto Serif is the text serif beneath it; a larger heading size would let the difference show.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-gambetta: Friendly and funky, Groovy lays rope-fine strokes into loosely tracked letters, its c nearly shut to a slit. Gambetta, a text serif, reads in a bookish, graceful way, its weight shifting gently from line to line.
gen-dafont-groovy-lora: Funky and friendly, Groovy draws true monoline letters with arms and legs of constant width, and a narrow slit for its c. Lora, a classic serif, brings sturdy hairlines and moderate stems, so the page has two distinct textures.
gen-dafont-groovy-noto-serif: Noto Serif, a text serif, reads with a restrained thick-thin look in every glyph. Over a long page that bookish rhythm settles in comfortably, while Groovy's wirelike, one-thickness lettering up top keeps things playful.
gen-dafont-halogen-fs-bespoke-serif: Sleek and quiet, Halogen looks drawn with a single pen tip, like a bent steel rod. Bespoke Serif adds authority beneath it, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones, so the heading stays crisp and the text feels dignified.
gen-dafont-halogen-fs-sentient: Sentient reads as sophisticated and contemporary, with pinched, closed-in apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than the stems. Halogen is best at sleek, laser-cut headings of a single cutting width, whereas Sentient does its finest work in the softer, finely shaded lines below.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-crimson-pro: Crimson Pro reads refined and classic, its letters packed close and its thick-thin cadence subtle. Hammerhead adds an industrial, laser-cut outline of one stroke width, and that gap between blunt and bookish is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-recia: Authoritative from both ends, Hammerhead draws a plain unmodulated outline with a generous e, while Recia, a classic serif, thins its arches only slightly where they leave the stem. Next to each other they feel firm and sharp, one blunt, one finely tuned.
